subject: Geography
central_question: How do environment, technology, markets and social organisation produce different forms of primary economic activity across the world?
in_scope_units: Meaning and environmental dependence of primary activities.
Hunting and gathering, including subsistence and market-oriented gathering.
Pastoralism: nomadic herding, transhumance and commercial livestock rearing.
Subsistence agriculture: primitive shifting cultivation and intensive subsistence systems.
Plantation agriculture and extensive commercial grain cultivation.
Mixed farming, dairy farming, Mediterranean agriculture, market gardening, horticulture, truck farming and factory farming.
Co-operative and collective farming as forms of farm organisation.
Mining, factors affecting mining and surface versus underground methods.
banned_topics: Manufacturing and industrial location, treated in Secondary Activities.
Trade, transport and service-sector activities, treated in later chapters.

known_pitfalls.claim: All primary activities are primitive and subsistence based.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter includes highly organised, capital-intensive commercial livestock rearing, agriculture and mining.

known_pitfalls.claim: Nomadic herding and commercial livestock rearing are the same.
known_pitfalls.correction: Nomadic herding is mobile and subsistence-oriented, while commercial ranching is permanent, capital-intensive, specialised and market-oriented.
Minerals near the surface are extracted by open-cast mining, while deep deposits require underground or shaft mining.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 3(i) comparing nomadic herding and commercial livestock rearing.
NCERT Exercise 2(ii) on the location of market gardening.
NCERT Exercise 1(ii) on successful co-operative farming.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with EXERCISES 1–3 and a Project/Activity requiring observation of crop cultivation in a nearby village.
